taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: 3 proposers ran in parallel, one per lens
4 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
The current HTTP Semantics specification is RFC 9110 (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html). I found no newer document that replaces it. All twelve codes are defined in its Section 15.

**Heuristic cacheability.** Section 15.1 names the codes defined as heuristically cacheable: "200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, and 501 in this specification". Of your list, that covers 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501. The sections for 303, 307, 413, 421 and 422 make no such statement and none of those codes is on the list, so they are marked false.

**Reason phrases.** 413 is now "Content Too Large" (it was "Payload Too Large" in RFC 7231). 422 is now "Unprocessable Content" (it was "Unprocessable Entity" in the WebDAV registration).

**Sources.** Every quote is taken from the code's own section of RFC 9110, and every url is the page I opened.
